definition: Data identifying individuals (names, IDs, contacts, biometrics, voice).
details: Data identifying individuals (names, IDs, contacts, biometrics, voice). LLM systems touch PII at every stage (training data, prompts, logs, outputs), triggering obligations under GDPR-style regimes and regional frameworks such as Saudi PDPL and UAE data protection law; PII detection and redaction pipelines are standard enterprise infrastructure.

explainer.lead: PII is data identifying individuals, such as names, IDs, contacts, biometrics and voice. It matters because LLM systems touch PII at every stage—training data, prompts, logs and outputs—triggering obligations under GDPR-style regimes and regional frameworks such as Saudi PDPL and UAE data protection law.

tiers.eli5: It is any information that can point to a specific person, like a name or phone number, and systems must handle it carefully.
tiers.practitioner: Enterprises build PII detection and redaction pipelines as standard infrastructure; a pitfall is overlooking PII in logs or outputs when focusing only on training data and prompts.
tiers.paperLevel: PII is data identifying individuals (names, IDs, contacts, biometrics, voice); LLM systems encounter it at every stage, and PII detection and redaction pipelines are standard enterprise infrastructure under GDPR-style and regional frameworks.

explainer.example: A redaction pipeline scans prompts and logs to remove names and contact details before storage.
